name: Emitter field, specular
description: The Cornell room with its ceiling light replaced by a 40 x 40 field of small one-sided emitters (0.03 m squares, 0.05 m apart; 3200 emissive triangles), whose radiance spans a factor of 64 in four levels and three tints. The emitters of one level and tint form one object. The white surfaces are glossy metal (roughness 0.2), which mirrors the emitter field, after the glossy scene of Shah et al.'s Figure 3. The hidden equal-time RIS projected-solid-angle benchmark renders it.
